blocks.title: Introduction
blocks.content:
The tenet of \emph{synthetic differential geometry} (SDG, cf. \parencites{Kock1979}{lavendhomme1996}{Kock2010}) is that concepts and results in differential geometry often find a more natural and powerful formulation after faithfully embedding the category of smooth manifolds into a suitable \emph{topos} (cf. \parencites{MacLaneMoerdijk1992}{Borceux1994III}) where \emph{infinitesimal spaces} exist as actual objects. 

\smallskip

GRIGORIOS GIOTOPOULOS, IGOR KHAVKINE, HISHAM SATI, AND URS SCHREIBER
Abstract. We have previously observed that the theory of solutions of par-
tial differential equations, regarded as diffieties inside jet bundles, acquires a
powerful comonadic formulation after passage from the category of Fr´echet
smooth manifolds to the Cahiers topos of formal smooth sets (a well-adapted
model for Synthetic Differential Geometry). However, the tacit assumption
that this passage preserves the projective limits that define infinite jet bundles
had remained unpro

blocks.content:
For reference in the main text, here we briefly record some basic definitions and
facts.
10 GRIGORIOS GIOTOPOULOS, IGOR KHAVKINE, HISHAM SATI, AND URS SCHREIBER
A.1. Formal Smooth Sets. We briefly review the topos of formal smooth sets
([Sch13, Def. 4.5.5; KS26, §2.1; GS25b, §2], exposition in [Sch25]), equivalent (by
[GS25b, §4.1]) to Dubuc’s Cahiers topos [Dub79; KR87], which is a “well-adapted
model” for synthetic differential geometry.
Our ground field is the real numbers. We write CAlg for the category of com-
mutative R-algebras.
